newsitem.title: USA: Long U.S. corporate bonds firmer, primary revived.
newsitem.headline: Long U.S. corporate bonds firmer, primary revived.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds were marginally firmer in longer maturities ahead of an early close on Friday, while new issuance resumed in the shadows of the Treasury's quarterly refunding effort, dealers said.

A drop in the U.S. Producer Price Index and flat read of industrial production affirmed a positive outlook for corporate bond investors, traders said, and buying out the curve firmed spreads. Still, overall volume was relatively thin ahead of an early close and a long holiday weekend.
"People have been looking to extend their corporate durations because they were caught short," one trader said.

The first sizeable new issues of the week were priced on Friday as the long bond yield pushed toward the psychogically important 6-1/2 percent level, syndicate officials said. Issuers were largely sidelined during the week as the taxable fixed-income markets were charged with digesting nearly $40 billion in U.S. government supply.

New issues were topped by $200 million short-term notes from Deere & Co's John Deere Capital Corp via lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co. The A2/single-A rated notes were priced as 6s to yield 6.013 percent or 23 basis points over the Treasury curve.

Also on Friday, Cummins Engine Co issued $120 million Baa1/BBB-plus rated 30put10 senior debentures as 6-3/4s to yield 6.792 percent or 50 basis points over the 10-year T-note. Goldman, Sachs & Co was lead manager.

Turning to high-yields, speculative grade companies capitalized on the cash-rich environment with the sale of about $1.0 billion in securities, including the second large venture satellite offering of the week.
TCI spinoff TCI Satellite Entertainment issued $352 million two-part debt through Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.

The B3/B-minus rated issue was comprised of $200 million 10-7/8 percent 10-year senior subordinated notes priced to yield 458 basis points over Treasuries and $152 million 10-year senior subordinated discount notes priced to yield 12-1/4 percent or 595 basis points over the curve.
The discount notes were priced with a five-year zero coupon.
Earlier, Dawson Production Services Inc issued $140 million B1/B-plus 10-year senior notes as 9-3/8s to yield 308 basis points over the curve via Jefferies & Co.
High-yield investors were also faced with a $500 million three-part Eurobond issue from Argentine telecommunications conglomerate CEI Citicorp Holdings SA via Merrill Lynch.

The deal included $100 million 8-1/2 percent five-year notes to yield 247 basis points over Treasuries, $225 million 9-3/4 percent 10-year notes priced to yield 352 basis points over and an Argentine peso 175 million 10-year tranche priced as 11-1/4s to yield 498 basis points over.
Standard & Poor's rated the first two tranches BB-minus.

High-yield secondary trade was nearly non-existent with the exception of one to two point losses in the $1.2 billion 11-1/4 percent Trump Atlantic City Funding Corp first mortgage notes, traders said.
The notes traded at 95-1/2 and 95, one trader said.
Trump Hotels & Casinos Resorts Inc on Friday reported a fourth quarter loss of $1.28 per share compared with a $0.48 loss of the same period one year ago.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association recommeded a 1400 EST/1900 GMT close on Friday and full close on Monday in observance of the President's Day holiday.
The Treasury bond closed up 17/32 to yield 6.53 percent.
